claim: The group's Capacity Reservation preference decides how reserved capacity is used: with capacity-reservations-only, instances fail to launch when no reserved capacity is available; with capacity-reservations-first, they launch as On-Demand instead.
question: What happens when no reserved capacity is left under the capacity-reservations-only and capacity-reservations-first preferences?

evidence.quote: The Capacity Reservation preference (`CapacityReservationPreference`) tells Auto Scaling how to consume Capacity Reservations when launching instances.
If no reserved capacity is available, instances fail to launch.
If no reserved capacity is available, instances launch as On-Demand.

note: Demand d56. The value names (capacity-reservations-only, capacity-reservations-first) are on the page as code labels before each sentence.

claim: With the Capacity Reservation preference none, Auto Scaling does not launch into Capacity Reservations and instances run as On-Demand capacity; with default, it uses the Capacity Reservation specification from the launch template.
question: What do the none and default Capacity Reservation preferences of an Auto Scaling group do?

values.display: uses the Capacity Reservation specification from your launch template

evidence.quote: **None** (`none`) – Auto Scaling does not launch instances into a Capacity Reservation.
**Default** (`default`) – Auto Scaling uses the Capacity Reservation specification from your launch template.

note: Demand d56. The display 'uses the Capacity Reservation specification from your launch template' is 9 words; a registrar may cut it to 'specification from your launch template'.

claim: A Capacity Reservation reserves EC2 compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone so that it is available when the Auto Scaling group needs to launch instances; when a Capacity Block expires, Amazon EC2 terminates the instances running in it.
question: Why would an Auto Scaling group target Capacity Reservations, and what happens when a Capacity Block expires?

values.display: Amazon EC2 terminates the instances running in it

evidence.quote: A Capacity Reservation reserves Amazon EC2 compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone, so that capacity is available when your Auto Scaling group needs to launch instances.
When the Capacity Block expires, Amazon EC2 terminates the instances running in it.

claim: An On-Demand Capacity Reservation used by an Auto Scaling group reserves compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone with no term commitment.
question: Does an On-Demand Capacity Reservation used by an Auto Scaling group need a term commitment?

evidence.quote: **On-Demand Capacity Reservations** – Reserve compute capacity in a specific Availability Zone with no term commitment.

note: Demand d56. Contrast for the reader: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans need a term; a Capacity Reservation does not (EC2 chapter owns the RI facts).

claim: An Auto Scaling group can use Interruptible Capacity Reservations: unused reserved capacity from On-Demand Capacity Reservations, or interruptible reservations shared through AWS Resource Access Manager, in exchange for accepting a 2-minute reclamation notice.
question: What is an Interruptible Capacity Reservation, and how much notice is given before the capacity is reclaimed?

qualifiers.scope: per instance in an Interruptible Capacity Reservation

evidence.quote: **Interruptible Capacity Reservations** – Unused reserved capacity from your On-Demand Capacity Reservations, or interruptible reservations shared with you through AWS Resource Access Manager, in exchange for accepting a 2-minute reclamation notice.

note: Demand d56. No document-history row or What's New item for this type was found in the ec2-auto-scaling change feed since 2022-07; its GA date is unknown here, so treat it as reference only, not examinable until dated.

claim: By default, Auto Scaling puts Availability Zone balance first when it consumes Capacity Reservations; with On-Demand fallback, instances launch as On-Demand in a zone without reserved capacity to keep the balance.
question: When an Auto Scaling group uses Capacity Reservations, does it favor zone balance or reservation use by default?

values.display: instances launch as On-Demand to maintain the balance

qualifiers.scope: per Auto Scaling group that consumes Capacity Reservations
qualifiers.condition: On-Demand fallback enabled for the On-Demand part of the claim

evidence.quote: By default, Auto Scaling prioritizes Availability Zone balance when consuming Capacity Reservations.
If reserved capacity isn't available in an Availability Zone, instances launch as On-Demand to maintain the balance.

note: Demand d56 and d18. To put reservation use before balance, the page points to the reservations then balanced strategy (GA 2026-06-30, not examinable yet; see ec2-auto-scaling-az-distribution-reservations-then-balanced).

claim: An Auto Scaling group's Capacity Reservation target can name only a single Capacity Reservation ID or a single Capacity Reservation Resource Group ARN.
question: How many Capacity Reservations can an Auto Scaling group name directly as its target, and how do you target several?

values.display: Only a single Capacity Reservation ID

qualifiers.scope: per Auto Scaling group Capacity Reservation target

evidence.quote: Only a single Capacity Reservation ID or Capacity Reservation Resource Group ARN is allowed as a Capacity Reservation target.

note: Demand d56. To use several reservations, the group targets a Capacity Reservation Resource Group.

claim: Since November 20, 2024 an Auto Scaling group can prioritize launching instances into Capacity Reservations through a Capacity Reservation preference set on the group.
question: Since when can an Auto Scaling group itself prefer Capacity Reservations when it launches instances?

values.display: prioritize launching instances into Capacity Reservations

evidence.quote: The Capacity Reservation preference (`CapacityReservationPreference`) tells Auto Scaling how to consume Capacity Reservations when launching instances.

| [Capacity Reservation preference](#DocumentHistory) | You can now prioritize launching instances into Capacity Reservations. For more information, see [Capacity Reservations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/use-ec2-capacity-reservations.html). | November 20, 2024 |

note: Demand d56; FRESHNESS item confirmed (2024-11-20). Current truth: ec2-auto-scaling-capacity-reservation-preference-values.

claim: Since November 7, 2024 you can choose an Availability Zone distribution strategy for an Auto Scaling group.
question: Since when can you choose an Availability Zone distribution strategy for an Auto Scaling group?

evidence.quote: | [Availability Zone distribution](#DocumentHistory) | You can now choose an Availability Zone distribution for your Auto Scaling group. For more information, see [Auto Scaling group Availability Zone distribution](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-availability-zone-balanced.html).  | November 7, 2024 |

note: Demand d18; FRESHNESS item confirmed (2024-11-07). The row does not name the strategies. Current truth: ec2-auto-scaling-az-distribution-balanced-best-effort and -balanced-only.

claim: Since October 31, 2023 an Auto Scaling group can launch instances into a Capacity Block for ML, which reserves GPU instances on a future date for short-duration machine learning workloads, by giving the Capacity Block reservation ID in the launch template.
question: Since when can an Auto Scaling group launch into Capacity Blocks for ML, and what are they for?

values.display: reserve GPU instances on a future date

evidence.quote: | [Capacity Blocks for ML](#DocumentHistory) | You can now launch instances into a Capacity Block by specifying the Capacity Block reservation ID when you create a launch template. With Capacity Blocks, you can reserve GPU instances on a future date to support your short-duration, machine learning (ML) workloads. For more information, see [Use Capacity Blocks for machine learning workloads](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/launch-template-capacity-blocks.html) in the *Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide*. | October 31, 2023 |

note: Current truth: ec2-auto-scaling-capacity-reservation-types-supported (instances end when the block expires). The capacity page now also allows targeting through a Capacity Reservation Resource Group.

claim: In the AWS example of an Auto Scaling group that processes images from an SQS queue, a fixed-size group works if the upload rate does not vary; if the number of uploads changes over time, AWS suggests dynamic scaling of the group.
question: When should a worker group that reads from an SQS queue use dynamic scaling instead of a fixed size?

values.display: you might consider using dynamic scaling

qualifiers.scope: per Auto Scaling group that processes an SQS queue
qualifiers.condition: the number of uploads changes over time

evidence.quote: The architecture for this scenario works well if the number of image uploads doesn't vary over time.
But if the number of uploads changes over time, you might consider using dynamic scaling to scale the capacity of your Auto Scaling group.

note: Demand d34 (with ec2-auto-scaling-sqs-backlog-per-instance-metric-math, ec2-auto-scaling-whitepaper-group-per-tier and ec2-auto-scaling-wa-queue-depth-metric-for-batch-work). No page in look_in states the word 'independently' for the web and worker tiers.
